genxml.title: VC1 video timing, cursor and display-ID controller on the Express board
genxml.doc: The same LSI Logic part as the Indigo Entry board's VC1 (see the newport repository's VC1 page for shared facts) reached through a different port set: seven word-strided ports in the graphics window instead of the REX1 function selector. It runs video timing programs from an external SRAM, generates the hardware cursor, and produces a per-pixel display ID from run-length tables in the same SRAM. Offsets are from the graphics window base (physical 0x1f000000 on the Indigo); each port is the first byte of a 4-byte stride, the command and SRAM ports are half-words. Grades: established means read in full in the shipped Indigo driver archive or PROM, or stated by a published document; inferred means a reasoned reading; unknown means nothing shipped settles it. [binary] marks a software expectation from a shipped binary, [public] a published document or public driver, [vendor-derived] a fact resting on the upstream headers only. Nothing was read on a board. Prose in devices/vc1-express/README.md.

struct.name: COMMAND
struct.doc: Internal register data port. Set the address pair to an internal register number, then write half-words; the address advances by two after each (cursor x then y are written back to back from address 0x22). Reads of this port never occur in shipped code (revision comes through testreg). [binary] A qtest can discriminate: address 0x22, write two half-words, check the address pair reads back advanced by 4 (inferred).

struct.name: XMAPMODE
struct.doc: Window to a display-mode table inside the VC1 (the Entry board's equivalent holds the mode words). Express keeps display modes in the XMAP5 chips instead. Unaccessed. Unknown.

struct.name: SRAM
struct.doc: External SRAM data port. The SRAM is addressed by byte; each half-word transfer advances the address pair by two. Written from timing images and display-ID tables; read back by the dummy-ID builder and Gr2SetMonitor. [binary]

struct.name: TESTREG
struct.doc: Revision read: after addrhi = 0 and addrlo = 5, the low three bits are stored as the VC1 revision. gfxinfo decodes 1 as A and 2 as B and every captured Indigo prints B, so the Indigo's part reads 2 (inferred from the decode and the captures; no direct read). [binary]

struct.name: ADDRLO
struct.doc: Low byte of the 16-bit address pair used by command and sram. Readable: the retrace shadow reads it back to save and restore the pair around interrupt-time use. [binary]

struct.name: ADDRHI
struct.doc: High byte of the address pair. Readable. [binary]

struct.name: SYSCTL
struct.doc: System control byte; readable (read-modify-write by the retrace handler and Gr2SetMonitor). Bit roles are NetBSD names [public] except as noted: 0 interrupt, 1 timing generator, 2 VC1 core, 3 display IDs, 4 cursor logic, 5 cursor display (established: toggled at retrace), 6 genlock (inferred), 7 video. Values seen: 1 at start, 3 during table loads, 0x0c final in the kernel, 0x3c final in the PROM. Bit 0 is the vertical-interrupt disable: set blocks the retrace latch, clear lets it set (the final values clear it; a comment on the value 1 in the IRIX source says it disables the interrupt) [binary][source]. qtest: with bit 0 set no retrace latch sets over a frame, with it clear one does.
